content: Clotrimazole is a medication used to treat yeast infections affecting the vagina, mouth, and skin, including conditions such as athlete's foot, jock itch, and body ringworm. It may also be prescribed to prevent oral thrush in certain patients. In some cases, it may be used for other purposes as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. Clotrimazole is available in various forms, including creams, lotions, and solutions for application to the skin; lozenges (troches) that dissolve in the mouth; and vaginal tablets and creams for insertion into the vagina. For oral thrush, it is typically used five times a day for 14 days. For skin infections, it is applied twice daily (morning and evening) for 2 to 8 weeks. For vaginal infections, it is used once daily at bedtime for 3 or 7 days. Always follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use clotrimazole exactly as directed, and do not use more or less of it or use it more frequently than prescribed. When using the topical cream, lotion, or solution, clean the affected area thoroughly, allow it to dry, and gently rub the medication into the skin until most of it disappears. Use only enough medication to cover the affected area, and wash your hands after application. Lozenges should be placed in the mouth and allowed to dissolve slowly over 15 to 30 minutes. Do not chew or swallow the lozenges whole. For vaginal cream or tablets, follow the instructions provided with the medication. Typically, you will fill the applicator with the cream to the indicated level or unwrap a tablet, wet it with lukewarm water, and place it on the applicator as directed. Lie on your back with your knees drawn upward and apart, insert the applicator high into the vagina (unless you are pregnant), and push the plunger to release the medication. If you are pregnant, insert the applicator gently. If you encounter resistance, do not force it; contact your doctor. After use, withdraw the applicator and discard it if disposable. If reusable, clean it with soap and warm water after each use. Wash your hands promptly to avoid spreading the infection. Vaginal cream or tablets should be applied at bedtime, as the medication works best if you remain lying down afterward. You may wish to wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Do not douche unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using clotrimazole even if you feel better. Do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. Use this medication during your menstrual period as well. If you obtained clotrimazole skin cream, lotion, or solution without a prescription, use it for 4 weeks for athlete's foot and 2 weeks for jock itch or body ringworm. If your symptoms do not improve within this time, stop using the medication and consult a pharmacist or doctor. If you obtained clotrimazole vaginal cream or tablets without a prescription and this is your first time experiencing vaginal itching and discomfort, consult a physician before use. However, if you have previously been diagnosed with a yeast infection and have the same symptoms again, use the vaginal cream or tablets as directed on the package for 3 or 7 consecutive days, preferably at night. If your symptoms do not improve within 3 or 7 days, contact your doctor. If your symptoms return within 2 months, also contact your doctor. Before using clotrimazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to clotrimazole or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease, immune system problems, HIV infection, AIDS, diabetes, or a history of alcohol abuse. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using clotrimazole, contact your doctor. Also, inform your doctor if you consume alcohol. If you forget a dose, take or insert it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one. Clotrimazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience itching, burning, irritation, redness, swelling, stomach pain, fever, foul-smelling discharge (if using the vaginal product), or upset stomach or vomiting (with lozenges). If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store clotrimazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Do not freeze it. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Clotrimazole cream, lotion, and solution are for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, and do not swallow the topical cream, lotion, or solution. Do not swallow the vaginal tablets or cream. If you have a vaginal infection, refrain from sexual intercourse. An ingredient in the cream may weaken certain latex products like condoms or diaphragms; avoid using such products within 72 hours of applying this medication. Wear clean cotton underwear (or underwear with cotton crotches) rather than synthetic fabrics like nylon or rayon. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the clotrimazole treatment, contact your doctor.
